consensus_summary: Primary identification of Israel as God's covenant people, most often the Church as true/spiritual Israel (believers by faith, Jew and Gentile), rooted in Jacob's renaming as one who strives/prevails with God; alternatives include distinct ethnic/national Israel, Christ as true Israel, or individual soul; no settled consensus across traditions.
book_summary: The new name of the one who prevails with God, defined by covenant and character rather than blood.
consensus_core_identification: God's covenant people (spiritual/true Israel or Church by faith, not mere ethnic descent)
book_core_identification: new name of the one who prevails with God (covenant and character, not blood)
boundary_disagreement: Book centers the individual who prevails and categorically excludes blood/descent, while consensus primary treats the collective people/Church as the main referent (with ethnic alternatives retained by some) and derives the spiritual criterion secondarily from the same texts.
rationale: Both cores rest on Gen 32:28 (prevailing/striving rename) plus Rom 9:6 (not all of ethnic Israel are Israel). The book preserves the non-ethnic, covenantal category that dominates consensus primaries but narrows the identification to the personal name-meaning and character criterion, thereby restricting extension to cases of prevailing character rather than the broader ecclesiological or national collective that consensus treats as primary.
strongest_objection: Book's singular focus on the personal rename and character criterion underplays the collective Church-as-Israel identification that forms the historical mainstream of the consensus primaries.
